about.title: Lindsay Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lindsay is a small city, but its citrus-packing warehouses, grocery stores along Hermosa and Tulare Road, and older apartment buildings all carry the same risk: an unaddressed spill, a broken step, or poor lighting in a parking lot can turn an ordinary errand into a serious injury. When a property owner or manager knew about a hazard, or reasonably should have caught it during normal upkeep, and did nothing to fix or warn about it, California law allows an injured person to pursue compensation for medical costs, lost wages, and other losses. The tricky part is proving what the property owner knew and when. Store and building surveillance footage often gets erased within days or weeks, and the physical evidence of a hazard, like a wet floor or torn carpet, can disappear before you even leave the building. We can move quickly to gather that evidence and evaluate whether a claim is worth pursuing, all free of charge to you.

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timing
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish this before they're lost or discarded.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Lindsay businesses overwrite security footage within days. We can send a preservation request quickly so the recording of your fall isn't erased before it's ever reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a share of damages. We can help present the full picture rather than let partial fault end the conversation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lindsay?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or municipal building in Lindsay, the deadline to act is much shorter, so it's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell on private orchard or agricultural property near Lindsay?
items.answer: Property owners, including agricultural operations common around Lindsay, still owe visitors a duty to address known hazards on walkways, entrances, and common areas. Whether a claim is viable depends on who controlled the area and what they knew about the condition. We can help sort out these details.

items.question: Do you charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You pay nothing to have your situation reviewed.
